storage.title: Cloud storage
storage.intro: Connect Dropbox once here; the connection is saved on this server and used by Dropbox sync. Two separate accesses keep sources safe: one can only read, the other may write only to output folders.
storage.readerHint: Read-only: used for every source folder. It cannot change anything in Dropbox.
storage.writerHint: Used only to publish into the output folders you choose; source folders are protected by the app.

storage.disconnectConfirm: Remove this Dropbox connection from the server?

storage.helpTitle: Where do I get an App key?
storage.help1: Sign in at dropbox.com/developers/apps and open (or create) your app with “Scoped access” and “Full Dropbox”.
storage.help2: On the Permissions tab tick files.metadata.read, files.content.read, sharing.read, account_info.read (and files.content.write for the write access), then Submit.
storage.help3: Copy the App key from the Settings tab into the field above. You can use one app for both accesses or a separate read-only app.

google.help4: Copy the client ID and secret into this page, save, then click Connect for each access.

reasonLong.network: The connection to the cloud storage dropped and did not come back within about 3.5 minutes. Nothing is wrong with the file; the next run tries it again.
reasonLong.download: The cloud storage refused the download (no access to this file).
reasonLong.protected: The PDF's own settings forbid copying its text (a permission set by its publisher, not a password to open it). Its text is not extracted. Keep an unlocked copy of it in the same folder, named like "name-已解锁.pdf", and that copy is distilled instead. You can also switch on reading such files from page images in Settings → Defaults.
reasonLong.covered: This room holds several copies of the same edition (a printed scan and a searchable copy, a protected original and an unlocked copy); only the best one is published, so this one needs nothing more.
reasonLong.duplicate: The input folder holds this exact file twice (same content, another place). It is distilled once, from the other copy.
reasonLong.unreadable: The file is damaged or not a valid document.
reasonLong.resources: The machine ran out of memory or disk space while reading it.
reasonLong.source_changed: The file changed in the cloud while it was read; the next run reads the new version.
reasonLong.unsupported: This file type is not handled yet.

help.title: What each state means
help.reasons: Why a file was skipped or cannot be processed

ok.means: Read and checked against its source; the accuracy meets the room's threshold.
ok.do: Accept it (alone, or with Accept all that qualify).

published.means: In the output folder, with who accepted it and when written into the file.
published.do: Nothing. A newer result replaces it only when someone accepts it.

below.means: Read, but the accuracy is under the threshold, or a number differs from the source.
below.do: Review it: compare with the source page, fix, and accept it if it is right.

skipped.means: Not needed: another copy of the same edition (or an identical file) is the one used.
skipped.do: Nothing. Show the original opens the copy that is used.

unprocessable.means: Could not be read. The reason is shown beside it.
unprocessable.do: Retry when the cause can go away (the network, memory); otherwise supply a readable copy.

processing.means: Being downloaded, read or checked now.
processing.do: Wait; the step and the time left are shown.

publishing.means: Being sent to the output folder.

email.resetDoneBody: Sign in with your new password.
email.notConfirmed: Confirm your email address first: open the link we sent you.

settings.hint: The mail server Fidelity uses to send confirmation and password-reset links. Any SMTP server works (company mail, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Tencent Exmail…).
settings.passwordSet: set — leave empty to keep it
settings.passwordKeep: Saved and encrypted. Type a new one to replace it; leave it as it is to keep it.
settings.siteUrlHint: e.g. http://10.0.0.150:8000 — left empty, the address people use is taken

ap.domains: company domains sign in at once; others wait for an administrator
ap.none: everyone signs in at once (as a viewer)

settings.off: Not set up yet: sign-ups wait for an administrator and forgotten passwords are reset by an administrator.

spot.hint: Each week 20 pages of the published library are drawn at random (fixed by the week, whoever opens it) and a person compares each with the same page of the original PDF. The error rate is judged by its upper 95% bound; the target is ≤ 1%.
spot.firstDraw: The first visit of the week draws the sample from Dropbox; it takes about half a minute.
spot.none: No sample page has been checked yet.
spot.result: {{checked}} pages checked, {{wrong}} wrong; upper 95% bound of the error rate {{upper}} (target ≤ {{target}}).
spot.needMore: {{n}} more clean pages are needed to show ≤ 1% statistically.
spot.above: Above target: look at the wrong pages
spot.ask: Compare word for word: figures, units, clause numbers and every table cell — do they match the original page?
spot.notePh: e.g. Table 5.3, second row: the page says 150 mm, the library 100 mm
